## Background

The **Valutazione della Qualità della Ricerca (VQR) 2020–2024** is the Italian national research quality assessment exercise conducted by [ANVUR](https://www.anvur.it/attivita/vqr/vqr-2020-2024/) (Agenzia Nazionale di Valutazione del Sistema Universitario e della Ricerca). It evaluates the quality of research outputs produced by Italian universities and research institutions over a five-year period.

Results were published on 28 May 2026. This report provides a transparent, reproducible analysis of how the **Department of Molecular Medicine (DMM)** at the **Università degli Studi di Padova** performed relative to peer departments within the university and nationally.

### What does the VQR measure?

ANVUR evaluates departments using three families of indicators:

| Indicator | Definition | Interpretation |
|----|----|----|
| **R** (quality) | Ratio of a department's average evaluation score to the national area average | R \> 1 means above-average quality |
| **H** (size-weight) | Fraction of expected products contributed by the department | Reflects the department's share of evaluated output |
| **IRD** (composite) | Product of H × R | Captures both quality and quantity — rewards large departments with high quality |

These are computed separately for three personnel categories:

- **R1**: Tenured staff (*personale a tempo indeterminato*)
- **R2**: Newly recruited / promoted staff (*neo-assunti / avanzamenti di carriera*)
- **R1_2**: All evaluated staff combined

::: callout-note
## Why does this matter?

VQR results directly influence the allocation of research funding (Fondo di Finanziamento Ordinario, FFO) to Italian universities, and are used internally for departmental benchmarking and strategic planning. A department's VQR performance has concrete financial and reputational consequences.
:::

## Executive Summary

::: finding-box
**DMM demonstrates strong research quality but is penalised by size in the composite IRD ranking.**

- DMM ranks **1st out of 32 departments** for R1 quality (1.26) — the best among all Padova departments for tenured-staff research quality.
- For overall quality (R1_2 = 1.15), DMM ranks **4th out of 32** — solidly in the top tier.
- However, because DMM is a relatively small department (157 expected products), its composite IRD1_2 (0.11) ranks only **21st out of 32**.
- This reflects a structural property of the IRD indicator: it scales with department size, so even high-quality small departments receive low IRD scores.
:::
